title: Tempo: which moves helped

D0.outcome: Explains a tempo as a move that helped development, and that moving a piece twice, retreating, or making a forced reply costs one.

D1.outcome: In a short opening line, marks which moves helped and which cost a tempo.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled opening positions, picks the line that gains a tempo (a capture that forces a recapture, a developing move that attacks a piece already moved) over the one that loses it.

D3.outcome: Predicts when the count misleads (wasted moves, exceptions such as a6 in the Ruy Lopez) and explains why.

misconceptions: Any piece moved twice is bad.
More moves made means ahead in time.
conditions: Open or semi-open openings with contact between the sides.
Both sides play sensibly; the pawn move is not forced by a threat.
contrasts: Counting tempi mechanically: a piece moved twice to win material or freedom is justified.
A6 in the Ruy Lopez and h3 are justified non-developing moves.
Closed games develop more slowly and allow more pawn moves.
